common_name: Diamond Snow Euphorbia (Compact Heat-Tolerant White-Flowered Filler Annual)

planting.note: Set out transplants after last frost in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Diamond Snow tolerates heat and humidity well, blooming continuously through the hottest part of a Gulf Coast summer.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade after frost danger passes. Diamond Snow is a compact, mounding annual euphorbia bred as part of the popular Diamond series, producing a dense cloud of tiny white flowers above fine, airy foliage, creating a baby's-breath-like filler effect that softens and fills gaps between bolder-flowered plants in beds, borders, and mixed containers. The tighter, more compact habit compared to the larger Diamond Frost makes it especially well suited to smaller containers and tight planting spaces. It blooms continuously from spring through frost with minimal deadheading required, tolerates heat and drought well once established, and performs reliably in the intense heat and humidity of a Gulf Coast summer where many other fine-textured annuals falter. Water regularly while establishing, then reduce frequency, since the plant prefers to dry out somewhat between waterings.

common_name: Lemon Coral Sedum (Bright Chartreuse Spreading Groundcover Sedum)

planting.note: Set out transplants after last frost in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; drought-tolerant once established and well suited to containers, rock gardens, and groundcover use.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade, since this succulent groundcover is intolerant of soggy conditions. Lemon Coral is a spreading sedum bred for its vivid, bright chartreuse-yellow, needle-like foliage that forms a dense, glowing mat or spills attractively over container edges, adding brilliant color contrast to mixed plantings even without flowering. Small star-shaped yellow flowers appear in summer, though the foliage color is the plant's main ornamental draw throughout the growing season. Highly drought-tolerant once established, it thrives on neglect and needs only occasional watering during extended dry spells, making it an easy, low-maintenance choice for rock gardens, green roofs, container spillers, and sunny groundcover areas where soil stays on the drier side.

common_name: Señorita Blanca Cleome (Sterile Spineless White-Flowered Cleome)

planting.note: Set out transplants after last frost in well-drained soil in full sun; sterile and non-seeding, so it blooms continuously all season without setting the messy seed pods of older cleome varieties, and will not self-seed or spread as a volunteer.

directions: Plant in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun after frost danger passes. Señorita Blanca is a sterile companion to the popular Señorita Rosalita cleome, bred to be entirely spineless and non-seeding, eliminating both the thorny stems and the prolific self-seeding that made older heirloom cleome varieties a nuisance in some gardens, while still producing abundant clusters of airy white flowers with long, delicate stamens from spring through frost. Because the plant never sets seed, all its energy goes into continuous flower production rather than seed development, resulting in exceptionally long, uninterrupted bloom without any deadheading required. The tall, bushy habit works well as a filler in mixed borders or as a temporary informal hedge, and it tolerates heat, humidity, and drought well once established.
